scoreEntries.title: README & Setup Documentation
scoreEntries.scoreHints: Comprehensive setup and usage documentation
scoreEntries.details: The README is strong: it explains what the service does, who it serves, how to run it locally with uv and PostgreSQL, how to run tests and linting, how deployment works, how configuration is sourced, key dependencies, ownership, personal data handling, and current limitations.

scoreEntries.title: Architecture Documentation
scoreEntries.scoreHints: System architecture and design documentation
scoreEntries.details: There is an architecture document, but docs/architecture.md is still a placeholder template and does not yet describe the actual runtime components, request flow, or deployment topology in a useful level of detail.

scoreEntries.title: Project Overview
scoreEntries.scoreHints: High-level overview describing the application's purpose, scope and audience
scoreEntries.details: The repository clearly states that this is the backend API for the Staff Self-Service Portal replacing Zendesk and KissFlow, and it explains the current feature scope, users, and the major items that are built versus still planned.

scoreEntries.title: Runbooks & Operations
scoreEntries.scoreHints: Operational procedures and troubleshooting guides
scoreEntries.details: There is some operational material in the README and a troubleshooting page exists, but docs/runbook.md is blank and the troubleshooting guidance is still generic. That leaves support and incident handling under-documented.

scoreEntries.title: Error Log Reference & Recovery Guide
scoreEntries.scoreHints: Common error logs documented with their meaning and recovery steps
scoreEntries.details: The repo documents health checks and some deployment troubleshooting, but it does not yet provide a concrete error catalogue or recovery guide for common production failures, request-id tracing patterns, or likely upstream dependency issues.

scoreEntries.title: Application Monitoring
scoreEntries.scoreHints: Comprehensive application performance monitoring
scoreEntries.details: The service has strong baseline observability: structured ECS JSON logs, per-request X-Request-ID propagation, Prometheus metrics, body-size protection, and optional Elastic APM integration wired into the app and Helm chart.

scoreEntries.title: Alerting & Notifications
scoreEntries.scoreHints: Proactive alerting on key metrics
scoreEntries.details: No alert rules, thresholds, escalation paths, or notification routing are documented in the repository. The monitoring document explicitly leaves dashboard and alert links to be added later.

scoreEntries.title: Health Checks & Dashboards
scoreEntries.scoreHints: Health endpoints and monitoring dashboards
scoreEntries.details: The implementation is good on probes and metrics: GET /healthz, GET /readyz, and /metrics are present and wired into Kubernetes probes. The gap is dashboards and documentation, which are not linked or described in a concrete operational way.

scoreEntries.title: Error Tracking (Sentry)
scoreEntries.scoreHints: Sentry integration added for error tracking and reporting
scoreEntries.details: I did not find Sentry configuration, dependencies, or integration code in this repository. Observability is centered on logs, Prometheus, and Elastic APM instead.

scoreEntries.title: Elastic APM Integration
scoreEntries.scoreHints: Elastic APM integrated for distributed tracing and performance monitoring
scoreEntries.details: Elastic APM is explicitly supported in app/core/observability.py and enabled by Helm values through ELASTIC_APM_SERVER_URL and related environment variables.

scoreEntries.title: Log Collection (Elastic Autodiscovery Annotation)
scoreEntries.scoreHints: Logs collected via Elastic autodiscovery annotation on pods
scoreEntries.details: The Helm chart enables Elastic log collection through pod annotations, and the application emits structured JSON logs to stdout in the format the platform expects.

scoreEntries.title: Monitoring Dashboard Links
scoreEntries.scoreHints: Links to monitoring dashboards added to catalog/documentation
scoreEntries.details: No Grafana or equivalent monitoring dashboard links are present in the README, docs, or Backstage catalog metadata.

scoreEntries.title: APM Dashboard Links
scoreEntries.scoreHints: Links to APM dashboards added to catalog/documentation
scoreEntries.details: Elastic APM is configured, but no APM dashboard links are exposed in repository documentation or Backstage metadata for operator use.

scoreEntries.title: Bugs
scoreEntries.scoreHints: Reliability issues detected by static analysis
scoreEntries.details: The service appears to be engineered with care: typed schema boundaries, many endpoint tests, real database CI coverage, and a passing Sonar quality gate badge. I did not audit the live bug backlog, so this is strong but not perfect.

scoreEntries.title: Vulnerabilities
scoreEntries.scoreHints: Exploitable security issues detected by static analysis
scoreEntries.details: The repo has Sonar analysis, linting, dependency management discipline, and a strong security posture in code and docs. I did not find explicit dependency vulnerability scan output in the repo, so this is high but not full marks.

scoreEntries.title: Coverage
scoreEntries.scoreHints: Percentage of code covered by automated tests
scoreEntries.details: Test coverage is a first-class part of the workflow: pytest runs in CI with coverage.xml preserved for Sonar, and the repository includes broad API and behavior tests across auth, tickets, dashboard, observability, storage, rich text, and attachments.

scoreEntries.title: Duplications
scoreEntries.scoreHints: Percentage of duplicated lines of code
scoreEntries.details: The codebase is split into clear API, schema, model, and service layers, which suggests duplication is controlled. I did not inspect a duplication report directly, so this stays below full marks.

scoreEntries.title: Code Smells
scoreEntries.scoreHints: Maintainability issues detected by static analysis
scoreEntries.details: The repo has consistent formatting, linting, strong inline rationale in tricky areas, and disciplined separation of concerns. The presence of placeholder docs and one or two operational gaps keeps this short of a top score.

scoreEntries.title: Hotspots
scoreEntries.scoreHints: Security-sensitive code requiring manual review
scoreEntries.details: There are clearly sensitive areas, especially auth, token handling, attachments, and personal-data workflows. The repository shows careful implementation, but I did not find evidence in-repo of formal hotspot review outputs or a completed security risk assessment.

scoreEntries.title: Security Scanning
scoreEntries.scoreHints: Automated security vulnerability scanning
scoreEntries.details: The repository uses Sonar and MegaLinter and has a clear security posture in AGENTS.md, but I did not find an explicit dedicated security scan stage for dependencies, containers, or IaC with surfaced results in this repo.

scoreEntries.title: Authentication & Authorization
scoreEntries.scoreHints: Proper identity and access management
scoreEntries.details: This is one of the strongest areas. Production authentication is Keycloak-only, route access is checked server-side, admin and HR permissions are explicit, and the code is careful about preventing development auth from leaking into production.

scoreEntries.title: Dependabot Automated Dependency Updates
scoreEntries.scoreHints: Dependabot PRs automatically created, reviewed and merged
scoreEntries.details: The README explicitly says there is a monthly Dependabot Python update PR, grouped into one PR. That demonstrates automated update creation, but not full automatic review and merge.

scoreEntries.title: Single Sign-On (SSO)
scoreEntries.scoreHints: Application secured with centralized Single Sign-On
scoreEntries.details: The production sign-in model is centralized Keycloak SSO, with OIDC flows, callback handling, token validation, and explicit configuration per environment.

scoreEntries.title: Support Documentation
scoreEntries.scoreHints: Support procedures and knowledge base
scoreEntries.details: The README contains useful operational context, but the dedicated runbook is blank and troubleshooting remains thin. Support documentation exists only in partial form today.

scoreEntries.title: Kubernetes Discoverability (Backstage)
scoreEntries.scoreHints: Kubernetes pods/workloads discoverable via the Backstage Kubernetes plugin
scoreEntries.details: The Backstage catalog metadata includes kubernetes label selector and namespace annotations, which is the correct setup for platform discoverability of workloads.

scoreEntries.title: ArgoCD Sync Status
scoreEntries.scoreHints: ArgoCD application sync status captured and visible
scoreEntries.details: The Backstage catalog metadata contains ArgoCD annotations, and the deployment model described in the README uses ArgoCD to deploy after CI updates Helm values.

scoreEntries.title: Feedback Channels
scoreEntries.scoreHints: Configured channels for collecting user/stakeholder feedback
scoreEntries.details: I did not find a documented feedback mailbox, service-desk route, Slack channel, or other explicit user feedback mechanism in the repository or Backstage metadata.
